t.1.53.1: When the sage Vasiṣṭha would not give up the wish-fulfilling cow, then, O Rāma, Viśvāmitra dragged away his Śabalā.
t.1.53.2: But Śabalā, being led away by the great-souled king, O Rāma, was distressed, and weeping, emaciated with grief, she pondered.
t.1.53.3: Have I been abandoned by the great-souled Vasiṣṭha, that I, wretched and sorely afflicted, should be carried off by the king's servants?
t.1.53.4: What wrong have I done to that great sage of purified soul, that the righteous one abandons me, though I am blameless, devoted, and dear to him?
t.1.53.5: Having thought thus, and sighing again and again, she then went swiftly to Vasiṣṭha of supreme splendor.
t.1.53.7: Standing before Vasiṣṭha, that Śabalā, weeping and wailing, spoke these words, her cry resounding like a thundercloud and a kettledrum.
t.1.53.6: Then, O destroyer of foes, shaking off those servants by the hundreds, she went with the speed of the wind to the feet of the great-souled one.
t.1.53.8: O blessed one, son of Brahmā, have I been abandoned by you, since the king's servants are leading me away from your presence?
t.1.53.9: Thus addressed, the brahmarṣi spoke these words to her, whose heart was scorched with grief, as if to a sorrowing sister.
t.1.53.10: I do not abandon you, Śabalā, nor have you done me any wrong; this mighty king is taking you away from me by force.
t.1.53.11: For my strength is not equal to his, and today especially the king is mighty: he is a kṣatriya and the very lord of the earth.
t.1.53.13: Thus addressed by Vasiṣṭha, she, skilled in speech, replied humbly with these words to the brahmarṣi of boundless splendour.
t.1.53.12: This host, a full akṣauhiṇī, is crowded with horses and chariots and thickly spread with elephants and banners; therefore he is the stronger.
t.1.53.14: They say the strength of a kṣatriya is no true strength; a brāhmaṇa is mightier. O brahman, the divine power of brahman is far mightier than the power of the kṣatra.
t.1.53.16: Command me, O greatly radiant one, filled as I am with the strength of your brahmanical power, and I shall destroy the pride of that wicked one, and whatever might he has.
t.1.53.15: Yours is strength beyond measure; Viśvāmitra, though of great valor, is not mightier than you, and your splendor is unassailable.
t.1.53.17: Thus addressed by her, O Rāma, the greatly renowned Vasiṣṭha then said, “Create an army that will crush the forces of the enemy.”
t.1.53.18: Sent forth by her bellowing cry of “humbhā,” Pahlavas in their hundreds, O king, destroy the whole army while Viśvāmitra looks on.
t.1.53.19: That king, utterly enraged, his eyes wide with fury, destroyed the Pahlavas with weapons of every kind.
t.1.53.20: Then, seeing the Pahlavas tormented by Viśvāmitra in their hundreds, she once more brought forth fearsome Śakas mingled with Yavanas.
t.1.53.21: The earth was covered with those Śakas mingled with Yavanas, mighty and of great valour, resembling golden filaments of the lotus.
t.1.53.22: By those warriors bearing long swords and paṭṭiśa spears, clad in garments the colour of gold, that entire army was utterly burnt up, as if by blazing fires.
t.1.53.23: Then the greatly splendid Viśvāmitra released his missiles.
